item.title: Request for safe, accessible pedestrian gate, 10th October
item.description:
Please could a proper, accessible pedestrian gate be installed here? This vehicle gate has had two metal bars removed to create a makeshift pedestrian opening. The route has been used for years by many people in the local area, but the current opening is unsafe and unsuitable for wheelchair users, pushchairs and people with limited mobility. Given how frequently the route is used, a proper pedestrian gate is needed to provide safe and accessible access.

item.title: Potholes and missing tarmac along alleyway from Hewlett Rd to Sidney St, 10th October
item.description:
The alleyway between Hewlett Road and Sidney Street has been in poor condition for approximately a year, and the situation is worsening. The pathway has broken and missing tarmac, numerous potholes and overgrown foliage along the edges, narrowing the available walking space. This creates a safety concern due to the uneven surface and potential trip hazards, while making it difficult for pedestrians, particularly those using prams or wheelchairs, to pass safely. The current condition also makes the alleyway unpleasant to use. Council request: Please arrange an inspection and carry out the necessary repairs to the damaged tarmac, fill the potholes and clear the overgrown vegetation. As the issue has persisted for a year and continues to deteriorate, prompt action is requested to address the safety hazards, improve accessibility and ensure the alleyway is safe for all pedestrians. Council request: Please arrange an inspection of the alleyway and carry out the necessary repairs to the damaged tarmac, fill the potholes and clear the overgrown vegetation. This is needed to remove potential hazards, improve accessibility and ensure the alleyway is safe and suitable for all pedestrians.
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 51a, Hewlett Road, Ewens Farm, Cheltenham, Cheltenham

item.title: Horses blocking public right of way, 10th October
item.description:
Field between Shaw Green Lane and Prestbury village/chuch/Mill Street. Landowner has horses grazing both sides of the fence dividing the field in two. Right of way is adjacent to the fence. Popular right of way to village. Half way across horses walked directly up to me and my dog which was on a lead. Other horses began to arrive. This is intimidating as horses can be dangerous to people and dogs. I had to turn and retreat as rapidly as i safely could. Another walker tool a large circuitous route across the field far from the path to avoid them. They are also sometimes to be found crowding the gates to the field. There is nothing to stop the landowner securing the horses on the other side of the fence to leave the path clear for walkers which is the situation that has prevailed over the summer. Can the landowner be asked to secure the horses and allow unimpeded walking over this public right of way please
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 36, Shaw Green Lane, Noverton, Cheltenham, Cheltenham
Report on FixMyStreet
